text.p: The Turkish lira was little moved in thin trade on Tuesday while bond market yields fell sharply due to strong demand in the Treasury's 13-month bond auction, the first ever, bankers said.
The lira closed firmer at 105,200 against the dollar on after Monday's 105,280 due to a lower dollar/mark parity.
Bankers said currency trade was weak and the lira moved according to the dollar's fall against mark in internatinal markets. It opened at 105,150 and slipped to 15,200 at close.

The central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory foreign currency transfers at 104,850 lira at the opening, after Monday's 105,050 lira close, but raised it to 105,000 as the dollar rose abroad.

The money market opened with a 4.2 trillion lira surplus. Overnight money traded at 77.50 and 77.75 percent for most of the day and the central bank lent 570 billion lira at 78 percent overnight at close, down sharply from the 14.6 trillion lira it funded overnight at 78 percent on Monday.

The central bank also fed banks 28.1 trillion lira via t/n value deals at 74 percent, up slightly from the 26.2 trillion lira it funded on Monday. It also lent 950 billion lira at 75 percent via tomorrow/week value deals.
Bond market yields dived by as much as four points across the board on a buying spree triggered by strong demand for the Treasury's 13-month bond auction, the first ever.
The Treasury sold 181.3 trillion lira of the 392-day bonds at 123.66 percent, down 12.66 points from the previous 9-month t-bill auction on December 3.

Bids totalled 478 trillion lira for the 13-month papers due to tax advantage, bankers said. The papers will mature on January 14, 1998, the longest maturity so far, and corporate tax on them will be paid in 1999.

The average yield on the most heavily traded June 4, 1997 paper sank to 110.72 from Monday's 114.95 percent. The second most active October 30, 1997 paper yielded 112.20, down from Monday's 116.09 percent average.
Banks will pay the Treasury 74.4 trillion lira for today's auction on Wednesday when 76.2 trillion lira will be cashed in from maturing t-bills.
